title: Hybrid headroom autoscaler: contract-aware allocation and soft-eviction
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a hybrid headroom autoscaler that is contract-aware (per-tenant throughput commitments), exposes soft-eviction pathways to preserve SLAs, and adds telemetry hooks for utilization and contract compliance. Opt-in via feature flag; safe rollback path included.
description: Summary: This PR implements a hybrid headroom autoscaler that combines predictive headroom (short-term demand forecasting) with contract-aware allocation. The goal is to reduce SLA violations during rapid surges while limiting overprovisioning for Dedicated customers with explicit throughput commitments. The change introduces a soft-eviction path that gracefully degrades non-contract traffic (best-effort) before affecting committed throughput. Motivation: multiple customers experienced transient SLA blips during microburst patterns; existing heuristics either over-provision or cause abrupt evictions. This PR balances cost and guarantees by adding an allocator that respects per-tenant contracts and a fallback pathway that applies graded throttles and reroutes to compatible model variants when necessary. Design highlights: - New allocator component: contract-allocator. It pulls per-tenant commitment metadata and current utilization, computes a desired headroom budget using an autoregressive short-horizon predictor, and issues reservations to the fleet headroom manager. - Soft-eviction flow: a three-step degrade path (throttle -> model-variant fallback -> enqueue-with-deadline) that is applied only to non-contract (best-effort) traffic and signals via a new header X-Redwood-Degrade-Reason for observability. - Telemetry & reporting: new metrics (contract_utilization_ratio, headroom_projection_ms, degrade_reason_counts) and a per-tenant daily compliance report (s3 export hook). - Config / flags: feature.hybrid_headroom.enabled (opt-in), allocator.lookback_ms, allocator.forecast_horizon_ms, degrade.window_seconds, degrade.priority_threshold. - Backwards compat: if feature flag is off, no behavior change. Contracts are read from existing tenant metadata store; defaults to 0 for tenants without commitments. - Performance: allocator runs in a lightweight event loop co-located with fleet-controller; forecasting uses an online linear model with bounded CPU. The runtime impact measured in local perf harness: median scheduling latency +1.8ms under steady state, tail +3.2ms at 99th (acceptably under SLO). Changes included: - service/autoscaler/contract_allocator.go: new allocator implementation and unit tests. - runtime/scheduler/headroom_manager.go: headroom reservation APIs and reconciliation loop. - runtime/scheduler/soft_eviction.go: degrade flows and decision engine. - telemetry/metrics_contracts.yaml: metric definitions and dashboards. - examples/ops/configs/hybrid-headroom.yaml: sample rollout config. - docs/operational/headroom.md: operational runbook and rollout checklist. - test/e2e/hybrid_headroom_test.go: end-to-end test harness simulating microbursts and contractual mixes. Commits: - 7f3d4b1: initial contract-allocator scaffold and interfaces. - 8a12d2c: implement short-horizon predictor and headroom reconciliation. - ae93b11: add soft-eviction decision engine and degrade pathways. - b44f0e5: telemetry hooks and dashboards (metrics + Grafana). - c1b9a9d: e2e tests and perf harness adjustments. - d2257aa: docs, feature flags, and rollout config. Tests & CI: Initial CI run had a flaky e2e that timed out under the nightly integration cluster (test harness timed out at 10m). Root cause: the test's mock backend used a fixed response delay; increased the harness timeout and added jitter to the mock to reduce coupling. After the fix, CI passed (unit, integration, lint, e2e). Review notes and conversation captured below. Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (canary): enable feature.hybrid_headroom.enabled=true for 1% of Dedicated nodes with no contract tenants; observe metrics for 72 hours. - Stage 2 (contracted tenants small cohort): enable for 5% of nodes serving pledged-tenants only; validate contract_utilization_ratio and no increase in committed-latency. - Stage 3: gradual ramp with automated rollback if contract_utilization_ratio falls below 98% or if degrade_reason_counts spike beyond thresholds. Monitoring / Alerts: - New alerts: ContractUtilizationDrop (P2), ExcessDegrades (P3). Both have playbooks in docs/operational/headroom.md. Known limitations: - Forecast model is short-horizon and will not capture multi-minute sustained ramps; for long ramps, normal autoscaler path remains primary. - Soft-eviction currently only degrades non-committed text-generation traffic; embeddings and synchronous admin routes are excluded. - Further tuning required for multi-region spillover heuristics. Related work: builds on ENG-1124 predictive-headroom prototype and reuses portions of throttle-orchestration (ENG-1421). Changelog & migration: no DB migrations; feature flag gateway ensures safe rollback. Merge: squash merge after approvals.

review_comments: Omar Rivera (requested changes, 2026-02-23): The allocator looks good but we should avoid calling the tenant metadata store synchronously on every reconciliation. Can we cache TTLs and instrument cache-miss metrics?
Maya Chen (author reply, 2026-02-24): Added an in-memory TTL cache with cache_misses metric; see allocator/cache.go (unit tested).

Tina Gupta (comment, 2026-02-25): Soft-eviction path needs stronger logging at the decision point to aid postmortems. Please add a structured event with tenant_id, reason, and pre/post utilization snapshot.
Maya Chen (author reply, 2026-02-26): Added structured_event emission and included it in the telemetry schema; updated docs with example logs.
Ethan Brooks (approved, 2026-03-01): Verified e2e on staging with 50% synthetic microbursts. CPU is within budget and contract SLAs held. Approving for merge.
